claim: The Anuradhapura-period maritime system was multi-port rather than dependent on a single gateway: Mantai/Mahatittha was a major north-western entrepot, Jambukolapattana served northern embarkation and landing, Gokanna connected the east coast to Bay of Bengal traffic, and Godavaya anchored a southern route; the importance and function of each port changed over time.
bounded_by: Do not treat all named ports as equally important or simultaneously dominant throughout the full Anuradhapura period. Uraturai becomes especially important later, including under Polonnaruwa.
notes: Run45 deepens the Run36 museum-map illustration by naming the port system and explicitly rejecting a one-port model.
